text:
Marta: dropping a quick question after the UX critique: should the undo window for rollbacks be 15s, 30s, or 60s? thinking about tradeoffs between recoverability and backend complexity.

Priya: 30s feels like a good default. gives humans a bit of breathing room but doesn't add much job orchestration complexity.

Oliver: +1 30s. also prefer the undo be clearly visible in the toast with a countdown and a tiny progress bar.

Alex (A11y): accessibility note: countdowns must not rely on color or motion alone. announce remaining time every 10s in a polite live region, and ensure the undo button is keyboard focusable. For SR users, saying "Undo available for 30 seconds" once is fine; avoid repeated verbose announcements unless user requests status.

Sam: backend: implementing a 30s reversible job is straightforward. 60s doubles the window but increases state churn. If we do 30s we can also add an account-level setting for teams that want longer windows.

Marta: good idea to make it configurable. UX question: do we show the undo toast in-context in the timeline, or as a global toast at top-right?

Priya: in-context is better — toast anchored to timeline gives clearer spatial mapping to the action. but also mirror a tiny global notification for users who navigate away.

Oliver: in-context + global mirror seems robust. ensure keyboard focus isn't stolen by the toast when it appears. it should be reachable but not auto-focus.

Alex (A11y): for screen readers: when the rollback completes optimistically, announce "Rollback applied. Undo available for 30 seconds." The undo button should have `aria-describedby` linking to the progress label. If user navigates away, the mirrored global toast should still be announced politely.

Marta: copy for toast: "Rollback applied — Undo (30s)" or "Rollback applied — Undo" with a separate time indicator?

Priya: I prefer "Rollback applied — Undo (30s)" so the timer is explicit. also add an accessible tooltip on the Undo showing exact expiry time e.g., "Undo expires at 14:33:05".

Sam: implementationally we can provide both: visible short timer and an aria-label on the button with expiry timestamp. frictionless to add.

Oliver: small motion nit: the toast progress should respect reduced-motion. in reduced-motion mode, switch to a numeric countdown instead of animated bar.

Alex (A11y): yes. also ensure contrast and that the undo target is at least 44x44 touch size on mobile. For keyboard, ensure tab order places undo reachable after the toast message text. Use `role=region` and `aria-live=polite` for the mirrored global toast.

Marta: what about multi-variant rollbacks? if user applied rollback to variant A and B at once, do we show a single undo for both or separate toasts?

Priya: single toast that lists affected variants is cleaner. e.g., "Rollback applied to Variant A, Variant B — Undo (30s)" Clicking undo reverts the whole job. If they want finer control, use the inspector.

Sam: agree. backend will tag jobs with affectedVariantIds so single undo is possible. separate undos per-variant would complicate job graph.

Oliver: telemetry note: we should capture undo rate and time-to-undo to inform defaults. add an event: `rollback.undo_shown`, `rollback.undo_clicked`, `rollback.undo_expired`.

Alex (A11y): testing plan: 1) SR reads optimistic apply and undo announcement 2) keyboard tabbing reaches undo and triggers it 3) mirrored global toast is announced if user moves focus away. I'll draft a 5-step checklist.

Marta: thanks all. I'll wire up Figma states for 15/30/60s and the mirrored-global + in-context designs. will attach the example ARIA attributes in the spec.

deploy-bot: preview created for feat/rollback-undo-window -> https://preview.redwood.dev/rollback-undo-window (expires in 24h)

Priya: i'll run a quick mobile check for touch size and mirror behaviour after your Figma update, @Marta.

Marta: plan: iterate on 30s as default, expose team setting for longer windows, add analytics, and include A11y test plan. will post updated prototype by EOD. :white_check_mark:
